entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antonio de Ferraris, also known by his epithet Galateo, was an Italian scholar, academic, doctor and humanist of Greek ethnicity.

Born in 1450 in the Republic of Ragusa, a Greek colony in the Adriatic, de Ferraris was raised in a culturally rich environment that would shape his future work.

He studied medicine, law, and philosophy at the University of Bologna, where he earned his degrees and became a renowned expert in ancient Greek literature and culture.

De Ferraris's most significant contribution was his collection of ancient Greek texts, which he published in 1517 under the title 'Colloquia Galatea'.

This collection of dialogues, written by the ancient Greek philosopher Plutarch, was a groundbreaking work that brought ancient Greek literature to a wider audience in Europe.

De Ferraris's legacy extends beyond his own work, as his publication helped to spark a renewed interest in classical studies and humanism during the Renaissance.
